cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz, who saw visions about Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1), is telling this one himself. It's the year King Uzziah of Judah died (2 Chronicles 26:1). And Isaiah says he saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted.

cards.question: Isaiah sees the Lord on a high, exalted throne. What fills the temple?

cards.text: Above Him stand seraphim, and each one has six wings. SIX WINGS, friend. I've got one mustache and I thought I was the most equipped guy in the room.

cards.question: Each seraph above the throne uses all six of its wings for flying.

cards.text: Two wings cover their faces, two cover their feet, and two do the flying. And the seraphim are calling out to one another about the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: These amazing creatures cover their faces in front of Him. What do the seraphim call out about the LORD of Hosts?

cards.text: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory." And then the building itself reacts.

cards.question: At the sound of the seraphim's voices, the temple's doorposts and thresholds stay perfectly still.
As the doorposts and thresholds shake, the temple is filled with ___.

cards.text: Isaiah cries out, "Woe is me, for I am ruined," because his eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts. I get it, friend: an important guest walks into my bakery and suddenly I see EVERY crumb on my apron.

cards.question: Standing before the King, what does Isaiah say about himself?

answers.text: He is a man of unclean lips
He is not a good speaker
He is the least in his family

cards.question: Isaiah says he is the only one with unclean lips, and his people are just fine.

cards.text: Then one of the seraphim flies to Isaiah, holding a glowing coal from the altar. He took it with tongs, and friend, I respect ANYBODY who reaches for the tongs.

cards.question: With the glowing coal from the altar, the seraph touches Isaiah's ___.
After the coal touches Isaiah, what does the seraph tell him?

cards.text: Then Isaiah hears the voice of the Lord: "Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?" That's the kind of question where a whole room suddenly gets REAL interested in the floor.

cards.question: The Lord asks whom He should send. How does Isaiah answer?

answers.text: He asks Him to send someone else

cards.text: Isaiah said yes. So the Lord tells him to go and tell this people to be ever hearing and ever seeing.

cards.question: In the Lord's message, this people keeps hearing and keeps seeing. What do they never do?

cards.text: Then the Lord says, "Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes."

cards.question: The Lord says that otherwise the people might see, hear and understand with their hearts. Then what might they do?

cards.text: Isaiah asks, "How long, O Lord?" Friend, I asked the dust in that junk drawer the same question every single day.

cards.question: When Isaiah asks how long, the Lord says only until the next king takes the throne.
The Lord says it lasts until the cities lie ruined, and the houses are left ___.

cards.text: And the Lord keeps going, "until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken."

cards.question: The Lord says that if a tenth remains in the land, it will be left alone.

cards.text: Then the Lord gives a picture: terebinth and oak trees being cut down.

cards.question: The Lord says the holy seed will be in the land like what felled terebinths and oaks leave behind. What is it?

cards.text: The holy seed will be a stump in the land: cut down, but still in the ground. Friend, I spent years worn down in the back of a drawer, and I'm here to tell you, STILL THERE counts for something.

findings.problem: Card 1 says Isaiah 'saw visions about Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1).' Isaiah 1:1 calls it 'the vision,' singular.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says the seraphim cover their faces 'in front of Him.' The text says they stood 'Above Him' (Isaiah 6:2). The wording also presents the face-covering as a reaction to Him, which hints at the answer 'holy.' The text gives no reason for the covering.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Card 7 ends with 'And then the building itself reacts.' That tells the baker the building does not stay still, so it gives away card 8, where the right answer is that the doorposts and thresholds do not stay perfectly still.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 7 cites only Isaiah 6:3, but its last line ('the building itself reacts') tells part of Isaiah 6:4.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The seraph's words 'your sin is atoned for' (Isaiah 6:7) are never told on any card. Only 'His iniquity is removed' comes up, as an answer. The atonement is a central detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Isaiah's answer 'Here am I. Send me!' (Isaiah 6:8) is the turning point of the passage, but no card tells it. It appears only as the paraphrased answer 'He offers to go himself' and as 'Isaiah said yes' in stop 2, card 1.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Most story cards in stop 2 have no Papa Dorin voice. Cards 3 and 8 are bare quotes with only a short lead-in. Cards 1 and 10 are flat summaries. The stop's weight can carry a reverent but present voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says 'The Lord says it lasts until...'. The word 'it' points back to the 'How long' question on an earlier card, which is no longer on screen. The question never says what lasts.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question changes the text's 'though a tenth remains in the land' (Isaiah 6:13) to 'if a tenth remains in the land.'
The wrong answer 'Nothing at all' is a different kind of answer from 'A stump' and 'A new forest.' It is an absence, not a thing left behind. That makes the answers uneven.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
